problem.summary: Closed-set detectors like YOLO are locked to predefined categories, while existing open-set methods either load heavy computation or deployment complexity; no single efficient model covers text, visual, and prompt-free prompts together.
statements: Closed-set detectors such as the YOLO series depend on predefined object categories, which limits flexibility in practical open scenarios where arbitrary objects must be recognized.
Open-set methods using text, visual, or prompt-free cues often compromise between performance and efficiency because of high computational demands or deployment complexity.
No single efficient model supports diverse open prompts (text, visual, and prompt-free) for arbitrary objects with both high accuracy and real-time efficiency.
Prompt-free detectors depend on large language models to name found objects, introducing considerable memory and latency costs.

evidence.quote: yet conventional models like YOLO series, while efficient and accurate, are limited by predefined categories, hindering adaptability in open scenarios

Recent open-set methods leverage text prompts, visual cues, or prompt-free paradigm to overcome this, but often compromise between performance and efficiency due to high computational demands or deployment complexity
Prompt-free ways, meanwhile, depend on large language models, introducing considerable memory and latency costs [33, 49]
Such scenarios increasingly demand models capable of detecting and segmenting arbitrary objects guided by diverse prompt mechanisms, such as texts, visual cues, or without prompt

background.summary: Builds on the YOLO lineage for speed and on open-vocabulary text-prompted detection (GLIP, Grounding DINO, YOLO-World), visual prompting (T-Rex2), and prompt-free generation (GenerateU); the claimed gap is that DINO-X is the only prior unified architecture but it is too costly to train and run.

solution.summary: YOLOE extends YOLOv8/YOLO11 into one efficient detection-and-segmentation model that accepts text, visual, or no prompts: RepRTA refines cached CLIP text embeddings with a one-block auxiliary network that folds back into the classification head, SAVPE encodes visual cues with decoupled semantic and activation branches, and LRPC turns prompt-free recognition into vocabulary retrieval without a language model.
solution.approach: Add three lightweight prompt modules (RepRTA, SAVPE, LRPC) on a standard YOLO architecture, re-parameterizing the text alignment into the classification head so inference is architecturally identical to closed-set YOLO.
components: Re-parameterizable Region-Text Alignment (RepRTA): one SwiGLU FFN auxiliary block refines cached CLIP text embeddings during training and is re-parameterized into the classification head for zero inference and transferring overhead
Semantic-Activated Visual Prompt Encoder (SAVPE): decoupled semantic and activation branches yielding low-dimension prompt-aware weights over multi-scale PAN features
Lazy Region-Prompt Contrast (LRPC): a specialized embedding filters anchor points by threshold, and only surviving points are matched against a built-in vocabulary instead of a language model
Object embedding head whose embeddings are contrasted with prompt embeddings to produce labels (Label = O . P^T)
Pre-cached MobileCLIP-B(LT) textual embeddings, allowing the text encoder to be dropped from training
Prototype-mask segmentation head trained jointly with detection in a single model
Staged training: 30 epochs for text prompts, 2 epochs for SAVPE with the rest frozen, 1 epoch for the prompt-free embedding

evidence.quote: For text prompts, we propose Re-parameterizable Region-Text Alignment (RepRTA) strategy
For visual prompts, we present Semantic-Activated Visual Prompt Encoder (SAVPE)
For prompt-free scenario, we introduce Lazy Region-Prompt Contrast (LRPC) strategy
which is identical to the original YOLO architecture, leading to zero overhead for deployment and transferring to downstream closed-set tasks

experiments.summary: Zero-shot evaluation on LVIS (Fixed AP on minival) for text, visual, and prompt-free prompts against YOLO-Worldv2, GLIP, Grounding DINO, T-Rex2 and GenerateU, plus LVIS segmentation APm, COCO transfer via linear probing and full tuning, FPS on T4 with TensorRT and iPhone 12 with CoreML, and ablations of RepRTA, SAVPE and LRPC.

evidence.quote: Notably, on LVIS, with 3× less training cost and 1.4× inference speedup, YOLOEv8-S surpasses YOLO-Worldv2-S by 3.5 AP
YOLOE-v8-M / L achieves 20.8 and 23.5 APm in the zero-shot manner
YOLOEv8-S / M / L outperforms YOLOv8-Worldv2-S / M / L by 3.5 / 0.2 / 0.4 AP

limitations.summary: The paper has no limitations section, but it admits that jointly learning detection and segmentation costs some detection accuracy (especially frequent-category AP), and that text-prompt training was shortened because of limited compute.
items: Joint detection and segmentation training in one model costs 0.2 AP and 0.9 APf in the ablation roadmap.
APf on LVIS for YOLOE-v8-M/L stays below YOLO-Worldv2, which the paper attributes to the multi-task trade-off of integrating detection and segmentation.
Text-prompt training was limited to 30 epochs (versus YOLO-World's 100 epochs) due to limited computational resources.

evidence.quote: Such multi-task learning introduces a trade-off that adversely impact detection performance on frequent categories, as shown in Tab. 5
Although this leads to 0.2% AP and 0.9 APf drop due to multi-task learning, YOLOE gains ability to segment arbitrary objects
Due to limited computational resource, unlike YOLO-World’s training for 100 epochs, we first train YOLOE with text prompts for 30 epochs

futureDirections.direction: Serve as a strong baseline that spurs further work on real-time, open prompt-driven vision tasks beyond detection.
futureDirections.quote: We hope that YOLOE can establish a strong baseline and inspire further advancements in real-time open prompt-driven vision tasks

deploymentClaims: After re-parameterization the model is architecturally identical to closed-set YOLO with zero inference overhead.
YOLOE-v8-S / M / L train in 12.0 / 17.0 / 22.5 hours on 8 Nvidia RTX4090 GPUs, about 3x less cost than YOLO-World.
YOLOE-v8-S reaches 305.8 FPS on T4 with TensorRT and 64.3 FPS on iPhone 12 with CoreML; prompt-free mode needs no language model.
